notes:
New units, charges that hit, fatigue, living ranks
- New unit: Spearmen. Longer reach (they strike first and keep swordsmen at spear's length), four different thrusts, spears held upright at rest. Braced spears stop a frontal charge dead: the chargers are thrown back and often hurt. Weaker in a long melee.
- New unit: Heavy Infantry. Two-handed greatswords, no shield, heavy armour: the hardest-hitting foot soldiers, slower and easier to hit back.
- Each army now fields spearmen, two regiments of swordsmen and heavy infantry.
- Swordsmen have more blows (an inward cut and a slash combo).
- Charges hit hard: the front of the charged line is driven back, some men are bowled over, and the charger's blow follows at once. Heavier and fresher men hit harder.
- Fatigue (Shogun 2): running tires a regiment in about 80 s and fighting in about 3 minutes; resting recovers. Tired men move slower, hit and guard worse, and charge softer. Shown on the regiment cards (Fresh, Winded, Tired, Exhausted).
- Living ranks: men waiting behind the fight now and then shout or raise their weapon, and the whole regiment cheers when an enemy unit nearby breaks.
- Right-clicking an enemy inside a melee now orders an attack even when one of your own men stands closer.
